title: Braiding equation for the canonical flat single tensorators
statement: Let B be a symmetric closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian coefficient category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions, X a scheme, and L,M flat sheaves on its small etale site. Write S for degree-zero inclusion and μ(L,M)=singleFunctorObjTensorIso(L,M).hom. Then the specified derived symmetry β(SL,SM) followed by μ(M,L) equals μ(L,M) followed by S of the ordinary symmetry β(L,M). There are no pairing maps or target sheaves. The notions are those of [def-kun-derived-tensor], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Symmetry is the canonical map of [lem-kun-tensor-sym].

source.place: Tags 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor and signed symmetry immediately following it); degree-zero specialization of the canonical tensor localization.

proof.text: For two single complexes check the braiding equation on tensor summands. Only the (0,0) summand survives. The Koszul sign (-1)^(0*0) is one, so the signed cochain braiding becomes exactly the ordinary sheaf braiding.

Apply the braided homotopy quotient and the defining braiding_hom_μ identity of Qh for the canonical derived braiding. Move the single/quotient comparisons through the braiding by naturality and cancel their inverses. The composite tensorator is exactly the flat single tensorator in the statement.

Use the explicit factorization of the flat single tensorator through the cochain tensorator, the homotopy quotient and Qh; its outer single/quotient components agree with the natural comparison. This identifies the computed square with the prescribed tensorators.

proof_origin.place: Canonical single-complex specialization of the tensor localization and its functorial comparison; expanded into the component argument above.

theorem singleFunctorObjTensorIso_symmetry
    (L M : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology B)
    (hL : ObjectProperty.flat L) (hM : ObjectProperty.flat M) :
    (((derivedTensorSymmetry B X).hom.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L)).app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) ≫
      (singleFunctorObjTensorIso M L hM).hom =
    (singleFunctorObjTensorIso L M hL).hom ≫
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map (β_ L M).hom
